Research profile

My research focuses on intelligent localization and embedded sensing, spanning multi-sensor state estimation, real-time pedestrian dead reckoning, and wearable positioning systems. I approach these problems through hardware–software co-design, considering localization accuracy, computational cost, energy consumption, and system integration.

Recent contributions include an embedded inertial positioning module, real-time motion estimation on IoT hardware, and a wearable–cloud architecture for continuous indoor–outdoor localization. My broader research interests include on-device AI and efficient learning-based methods for positioning on resource-constrained platforms.

I received my Ph.D. in Computer Science from KAIST in 2026, following an M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering from KAIST in 2020. Earlier research addressed LoRa-based sensing and control for agriculture and machine learning for Vietnamese Sign Language translation.

Research interests

  • Intelligent localization & navigation
    Continuous indoor–outdoor positioning, pedestrian dead reckoning, and map-aware localization in environments with limited or unreliable GNSS coverage.
  • Multi-sensor fusion & on-device AI
    Real-time estimation from heterogeneous sensor data, with a research interest in efficient learning-based localization on embedded devices.
  • Embedded systems & industrial IoT
    Hardware–software co-design and device–cloud architectures for wearable navigation, connected sensing, and location-based safety management.
